current.title: The World Is Quietly Running Out Of Sand
current.hook: Sand is vanishing five times faster than in 1970, and you're standing on it.
current.closing: Somehow, the beach is the crisis.
current.question: Could sand really run out? Comment below.

problems: seg2 never shows the 13B rivers replace, so the core 4x claim is spoken but not demonstrated.
seg1 timeline occupies a thin strip with large empty dark areas above and below; Data just stands arms-up on a dot.
seg3/seg4 reuse the same ranked-bar chart; Data stands on the China bar and covers the 51% label (seg3:end, seg4:end).
The 'China 51' map label is clipped and collides with the map. The fifth row 'United States o...' is truncated, with its value cut off by the panel edge.
Nothing anywhere looks like sand. Slabs, tiles and bars could be any commodity.
The closing 'Somehow, the beach is the crisis' has no visual payoff. It is the same bar chart with a caption.
fixes: Rebuild seg2 as a riverbank: the river deposits 13 heaps while Data shovels out 50, so the shore visibly erodes four times faster than it refills.
Make seg0's blocks read as sand: heaps or bags with grain texture that Data pours or shovels. Show the 1970 pile beside today's pile at 1/5 the height.
Replace the seg1 timeline with a growing sand pile or dune that uses the full frame height.
Keep Data off the bars' value labels. Have him pour cement or sand into China's bar to make it rise to 51%.
Give the closing a beach picture, such as a shoreline receding as Data digs, instead of reusing the bar chart.
Fix the clipped 'China 51' label and the truncated 'United States o...' row.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
